title: Tool spec gatekeeper and async resume invoker for cross-SDK function calls
creator: Anika Patel
description: Build a runtime-side 'gatekeeper' and accompanying cross-SDK helper (Python/TS/Go) that perform progressive function-schema validation and manage resumable streaming invocation for tool/function calls. Goals: 1) provide tolerant, explainable schema reconciliation at invocation time so older SDK clients and newer model-declared schemas interoperate; 2) surface deterministic validation errors with recovery hints; 3) implement an async-resume invoker that can resume a function call stream after transient network interruptions or partial responses, preserving KV-cache continuity where applicable; 4) expose ergonomic client-side wrappers and generated type-safe bindings for each SDK so customer code can call tools with predictable retries and streaming semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Gatekeeper accepts a model-declared function schema and client-supplied call payload and returns: VALID, RECOVERABLE_WARNING (with suggested coercions), or INVALID with a deterministic error code and human-friendly message.

SDK helpers in Python, TypeScript, and Go provide a single-call API 'invoke_tool_resumable' that supports: streaming partial results, automatic retry on idempotent stages, and explicit resume tokens returned by the runtime.
Resume tokens are stable across short-lived restarts and include minimal opaque metadata; SDKs must encrypt tokens at-rest when persisted by client code (examples provided).

End-to-end integration tests cover: schema mismatch with suggested coercion flows, network interruption mid-stream with automatic resume, and a forced partial-success where client performs manual reconciliation.
Benchmarks show less than 10% P99 added latency for non-streaming calls when the gatekeeper is enabled; streaming throughput unaffected beyond negligible headers (<=1% token overhead).
Design doc and cross-SDK examples published; API docs and migration guide available in the SDK repos and Console docs.
technical_notes: Key ideas: implement reconcilers that try ordered strategies: strict validation -> type coercion (numbers from strings, truncated arrays with warnings) -> default injection (if declared default present) -> reject. Each step emits a structured explanation string for the SDK to surface. The async resume invoker composes three primitives: checkpointing (per-call resumable sequence id), idempotent boundary markers (for multi-stage toolchains), and 'stream continuation' handshake (client presents resume token; server answers with next seq index or full re-send). For KV cache continuity, we propagate glob-tagged KV keys to runtime to reconstruct decoder caches; any incompatibility triggers a safe-fallback path that replays minimal state with rate-limited token cost accounting.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Spec and design (2 days) - finalize gatekeeper state machine, token format, and coercion strategies; design SDK facade API surfaces.
Phase 2: Runtime prototype (5 days) - implement gatekeeper validator library and a resumable stream handler in the serving runtime; add feature flag 'fn_resumable_v1'.
Phase 3: SDK integrations (7 days parallel per language) - add invoke_tool_resumable in Python/TS/Go, include utility to persist/resume tokens, and ship example apps.
Phase 4: E2E tests and benchmarks (3 days) - fault injection tests (mid-stream TCP drop, process restart), latency/cost profiling.
Phase 5: Docs, migration guide, and rollout (2 days) - Console docs, SDK changelogs, and gradual rollout via feature flag + canary customers.
qa_notes: Create mocks that simulate: schema evolution (new optional params, renamed keys with alias map), partial JSON emission, and token corruption scenarios.
Validate resume semantics under these conditions: reconnect after 1s, 10s, and 3m; verify resume token expiry is enforced per design (default 10 minutes).
Add fuzz tests that send large arrays and non-conforming types to ensure gatekeeper returns RECOVERABLE_WARNING rather than silently coercing when unsafe.
tests: Integration: SDK invoke_tool_resumable against runtime test instance with stepwise failures
E2E: replay logs from a past customer incident and confirm resume path yields identical final tool output
Performance: P50/P95/P99 comparisons with gatekeeper on/off for 10k synthetic calls
updates: 2026-03-06: Kickoff meeting — agreed to use opaque resume token format and 10-minute default TTL. Liam volunteered to own token design. Action: prototype token handshake spec.
2026-03-08: Prototype runtime gatekeeper implemented; initial coercion strategies logged. Early tests show numeric coercion recovers ~12% of real-world mismatches from customer traces.
2026-03-09: Cross-SDK API review — PM requested a single async call entrypoint to reduce surface area; decided on 'invoke_tool_resumable' with language idiomatic signatures.

2026-03-10: Design review — Security flagged persisted tokens as sensitive; requirement added: SDK example must show encryption before storing on-disk. Security review required flag updated in ticket.
2026-03-11: TS helper PR created; initial tests pass but race observed when resume tokens are used concurrently from two threads — creating a mutex recommendation in helper docs.
2026-03-12: Runtime PR added feature-flag 'fn_resumable_v1' behind canary; benchmark shows 6% overhead on non-streamed calls. Flag default off for now.
